title: Python Memory Management & GIL
source: IBM SkillsBuild Advanced Python Engineering Handbook
content: Python uses automatic memory management based on reference counting and a cyclic garbage collector. In CPython, the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) is a mutex that prevents multiple native threads from executing Python bytecode simultaneously. For CPU-bound workloads, use multiprocessing or concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor to bypass GIL constraints.
key_takeaways: GIL synchronizes thread access to CPython internal state
Use multiprocessing for CPU-bound tasks and async/threading for I/O-bound tasks

title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Principles & SOLID
content: The four pillars of OOP are Encapsulation (bundling data and methods), Abstraction (hiding implementation complexity), Inheritance (reusing code across parent-child hierarchies), and Polymorphism (dynamic method overriding/overloading). The SOLID principles ensure scalable design: Single Responsibility, Open-Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.
key_takeaways: SOLID principles prevent tight coupling and brittle architectures
Dependency Injection promotes loose coupling and testability

title: RESTful API Design & HTTP Status Codes
content: REST APIs rely on stateless client-server communication using standard HTTP verbs: GET (read/idempotent), POST (create/non-idempotent), PUT (replace/idempotent), PATCH (partial update), and DELETE (remove/idempotent). Common status code families: 2xx (Success, 200 OK, 201 Created), 4xx (Client Error, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found), 5xx (Server Error, 500 Internal Error, 503 Service Unavailable).
key_takeaways: Strict status code semantics for client predictability
